findings.source_en: And yet, you’ve defiled it with this rabble.
findings.issue: 'it' is the sacred ground named in the immediately preceding line of the same node (كُلّفتَ بحماية هذه الأرض المقدسة). الأرض is feminine, so the pronoun must be ـها; دنّستَه points at a masculine antecedent that does not exist in the scene.

Undiacriticized لست نبيًا reads equally as لستُ (I am no prophet) and لستَ (you are no prophet). Both speakers are in this exchange - Smert confessing and the Sester who has just called him 'Prophet Smert' - so the attribution flips depending on how the reader vowels it.
The previous line already renders 'a sign' as علامة. Repeating علامة for 'An omen' collapses the source's escalation (sign -> omen -> anything) into the same word twice.
